title: CS50: Introduction to Computer Science
duration: About 11 weeks, at your own pace
description:
Harvard's well-known first course in programming and computer science. It starts from zero and moves through C, Python, SQL and web development, with weekly problem sets.

Best for: Complete beginners who have never written code; First-year and second-year students who want a strong base; Anyone switching to tech from another field
What you get: Recorded lectures and notes, free to follow; Weekly problem sets that make you build real programs; A very active online community; Certificate options are explained on the course page

title: CS50's Introduction to Programming with Python
duration: About 10 weeks, at your own pace
description:
A shorter, Python-only course from the CS50 team. Good if you want to learn Python properly before a data, automation or backend internship.

Best for: Beginners who want to learn Python first; Students preparing for data or backend internships
What you get: Video lectures and notes; Problem sets with automatic checking; Python basics up to files, libraries and testing; Certificate options are explained on the course page

title: freeCodeCamp: Full web development curriculum
duration: Self-paced, hundreds of hours in total
description:
A free, project-based curriculum that covers HTML, CSS, JavaScript, responsive design, APIs and more, with coding exercises you solve right in the browser.

Best for: Beginners who learn best by building; Students who want projects for their resume; Self-learners without a laptop setup (it runs in the browser)
What you get: Interactive coding exercises in the browser; Projects you can show to employers; Free certifications after finishing the projects; A large community forum

title: Kaggle Learn: short courses in Python, Pandas, SQL and machine learning
duration: A few hours per course, at your own pace
description:
Short, practical courses with notebooks you run in the browser. Each one focuses on a single skill, so you can finish one in a weekend.

Best for: Students aiming for data analyst or data science internships; Learners who want quick, hands-on practice; Anyone who already knows a little Python
What you get: Hands-on notebooks that run in the browser; Short courses on Python, Pandas, SQL, data visualization and machine learning; A free certificate of completion for each course

title: Microsoft Learn: free learning paths for developers, data and cloud
duration: Self-paced, from 30 minutes to many hours
description:
Free tutorials and learning paths from Microsoft on programming, Azure, data, AI and Office tools, with sandbox exercises that need no setup.

Best for: Students aiming for cloud, data or software roles; Learners preparing for a Microsoft certification; Beginners who like step-by-step guided paths
What you get: Guided learning paths with exercises; Free sandbox environments for practice; Progress tracking and achievements on your profile

title: NPTEL: free courses from the IITs and IISc
description:
A national programme that offers recorded and live-run university courses from the IITs and IISc in engineering, science, management and the humanities. Learning is free; an optional paid exam is how you earn a certificate.

Best for: Engineering and science students who want IIT-level teaching; Students who want a recognised certificate for their resume; Learners who like a fixed weekly schedule
What you get: Video lectures and course material at no cost; Weekly assignments; An optional proctored exam for a certificate (exam fee applies, check the course page)

title: SWAYAM: free online courses from Indian universities
description:
The Government of India's platform for online courses from Indian universities and institutes, from school level up to postgraduate. Some courses count as credit transfer in many universities.

Best for: College students who want extra credits or subjects; Learners who want courses from Indian institutions; Students who prefer a structured semester-style course
What you get: Free video lectures and reading material; Quizzes and assignments; An optional exam for a certificate (fee applies, check the course page)

title: The Odin Project: full-stack web development path
description:
An open-source curriculum that teaches web development using real tools (the terminal, Git, VS Code) and lots of projects. It pulls together the best free material instead of lecturing itself.

Best for: Learners who want a serious, project-heavy path; Students aiming for web developer internships; People comfortable studying on their own
What you get: A complete path from HTML to full-stack JavaScript; Many portfolio projects you can show; An active chat community for help

title: IBM SkillsBuild: free courses in AI, data, cybersecurity and workplace skills
description:
IBM's free learning platform with courses for students and early-career learners, including AI, data analytics, cybersecurity, cloud and professional skills. Completed courses earn digital credentials.

Best for: Students and freshers exploring tech careers; Learners who want a credential to add to LinkedIn; Beginners who want career-readiness skills alongside tech
What you get: Free courses and learning plans; Digital badges or credentials on completion; Career-readiness material such as resume and interview help

title: Google Cloud Skills Boost: hands-on cloud labs and learning paths
duration: Self-paced labs from minutes to hours
description:
Hands-on labs and learning paths for Google Cloud, with a real cloud environment opened for each lab. Some content is free; some needs credits or a subscription, so check the page before you start.

Best for: Students aiming for cloud or DevOps internships; Learners who want to practice, not only watch videos; People who have basic programming knowledge
What you get: Real cloud labs with temporary accounts; Learning paths and skill badges; Free and paid content (check what is free before starting)

title: Skills for All: free Cisco courses in networking, cybersecurity and Python
description:
Free self-paced courses from Cisco Networking Academy covering networking basics, cybersecurity, programming and digital skills, with badges when you complete them.

Best for: Students interested in networking or cybersecurity; Beginners who want a clear, structured start; Learners who want a badge to show on their profile
What you get: Free self-paced courses; Hands-on activities and quizzes; Badges or certificates of completion

title: Khan Academy: free maths, science, economics and computing lessons
description:
Free lessons, practice questions and quizzes, from school maths to statistics, economics and introductory computer programming.

Best for: School and first-year college students who need to revise the basics; Anyone who wants to fix weak maths or statistics before a data course; Learners who like short videos with practice questions
What you get: Short video lessons; Practice questions with instant feedback; Progress tracking

title: MIT OpenCourseWare: free lecture notes, videos and problem sets
description:
Material from real MIT courses, including lecture videos, notes, assignments and exams across computer science, maths, engineering and business. There is no certificate or teacher support, so it suits disciplined self-learners.

Best for: Strong self-learners who want university-level depth; Students who want extra material for their own degree; Learners who are happy without a certificate
What you get: Lecture videos and notes at no cost; Assignments and past exams to practice with; No sign-up needed to read the material

title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python (free to read online)
description:
A beginner-friendly book, free to read online, that teaches Python through practical tasks such as working with files, spreadsheets, PDFs and web pages.

Best for: Complete beginners who like practical examples; Students in non-tech courses who want to automate everyday work; Anyone who finds theory-heavy courses dull
What you get: A full beginner Python book, free online; Practice projects that save real time; Skills useful in office, operations and analyst roles

title: Hugging Face Learn: free courses on modern machine learning and AI
description:
Free courses from Hugging Face on natural language processing, large language models and related areas, with code you can run and change.

Best for: Students who already know Python and want to try AI; Learners aiming for machine learning internships; People who want to build small AI projects
What you get: Free courses with runnable code; Hands-on practice with real models and datasets; A community to ask questions

title: Skill India Digital Hub: free skilling courses and certificates
description:
The Government of India's skilling platform with courses in many trades and digital skills, including options linked to national skill certification. Check each course page for what certificate it gives.

Best for: Students and school leavers looking for job-ready skills; People who want a government-recognised skill certificate; Learners interested in trades as well as tech
What you get: Free skilling courses; Certificates for selected courses (see each course page); A single place to find government skilling schemes

title: Junior Analyst, Risk Management
description:
Razorpay is one of India’s leading full-stack financial technology companies, powering the way businesses move, manage, and grow money. Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar with a simple vision - to simplify payments for Indian businesses - we’ve since grown into a fintech powerhouse driving India’s digital payment revolution.
 Razorpay powers millions of businesses with a smarter, scalable stack that goes beyond transactions to help them truly build and grow.
 From building AI-native agentic payments, to AI-assisted fraud detection and real-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. In close collaboration with ecosystem partners - including banks, networks, regulators - we are pioneering industry-first solutions that are shaping the next era of fintech
 Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation - powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia.
 Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently.
 Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme - and over 100 of India’s unicorns. With strong roots in India and growing operations in Southeast Asia, we are shaping the next chapter of financial technology across the region.
 We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India & SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions - including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards-first UPI) - along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia.
 But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen - you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle - if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People > Pedigree - we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. Transparency thrives over titles - this is where interns question CXOs and CXOs say “thank you.” Guided by our values of Customer First, Autonomy & Ownership, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Challenging the status quo and a strong belief that Razorpay grows with Razors, you’ll be part of a 3000+ strong team building not just products, but the financial infrastructure of the future.
 Title - Junior Analyst - Risk Management 
 About Razorpay 
 In 2014, what started as India’s first payment gateway built for startups is now one of India’s youngest FinTech unicorns with a $8 billion valuation and the single best destination for all things payments and business banking. Razorpay offers an integrated platform for all things payments and business banking, helping millions of small and large businesses simplify and accelerate every aspect of their financial journey.
 Today, Razorpay is a 2500-fun bunch of spirited, analytical, and ambitious folks building first-of-its-kind technologies for the fintech ecosystem. We are a bunch of hungry mavericks here to empower 8 million businesses in their digital transformation and enhance the payment experience of over 500 million end consumers in the next twelve months.
 And we are just getting started. Come and join this club of thinkers, innovators, dreamers, and challengers.
 Roles and Responsibilities 
 Monitor transactions/ merchants to identify risk/fraud and take necessary action immediately. 
 Handle transaction queries in case of discrepancies where disputes arise from the customer.
 Work closely with the partner banks and Cybercell to handle chargebacks/customer disputes and ensure timely recovery to reduce losses.
 Speak to merchants or customers to understand and address queries/concerns.
 Identify innovative ways to reduce risks by providing inputs on enhancing the process and reduce monetary losses . 
 Skills and Experience 
 Bachelor's Degree.Freshers, knowledge about a customer support app or CRM , such as freshdeskKnowledge of Stages/levels of chargebacks, penalty involved at the arbitration stage, technical chargebacks, Visa/Mastercard guidelines in brief, reason code in relation to fraud chargebacks.Interpersonal skills
 Friendly and pleasant demeanor over phone and email Communication skills 
 Exceptional verbal and written communication Listening skills - Understand, anticipate and resolve queries arising from various stakeholders Attention to detail and accuracy - Excellent orgaizational skills and multitasking skills. Identify anomalies or suspicious behaviours.
 Razorpay believes in and follows an equal employment opportunity policy that doesn't discriminate on gender, religion, sexual orientation, colour, nationality, age, etc. We welcome interests and applications from all groups and communities across the globe. 
 Follow us on LinkedIn & Twitter

title: Associate - Motor Insurance
description:
Sales Executive / Sr. Sales Executive — Motor Insurance
Department: Paytm Insurance Broking | Location: Noida, Uttar Pradesh
Experience: 0 months – 5 years | Employment Type: Full-time
Role Overview The Sales Executive / Sr. Sales Executive (Motor Insurance) will be responsible for driving sales of motor insurance products (Two-Wheeler, Private Car, and Commercial Vehicle policies). The ideal candidate will be adept at converting leads, understanding customer vehicle insurance needs, and generating insights that help refine lead quality and sales strategies.

Key Responsibilities
Generate and convert telesales leads specifically for motor insurance products (Two-Wheeler, Four-Wheeler, and Commercial Vehicles).
Maintain an in-depth understanding of motor insurance features, benefits, add-on covers (Zero Dep, Engine Protect, RSA), and policy terms across multiple insurers.
Identify potential customers through cold calling, renewals, referrals, or digital leads provided by the organization.
Engage with customers to understand their vehicle insurance requirements and recommend the best-fit policies.
Assist customers with seamless policy issuances, rollovers, and renewal conversions.
Achieve daily, weekly, and monthly motor insurance sales targets.
Provide regular feedback on lead quality, conversion ratios, and customer sentiment to improve overall sales efficiency.
Prepare and maintain sales reports, pipeline updates, and conversion data in CRM tools.
Stay updated on motor insurance industry trends, new product offerings, and IRDAI regulatory changes.

Key Skills & Competencies
Strong communication, negotiation, and persuasion skills.
Sound knowledge of motor insurance concepts (IDV, NCB transfers, Third-Party vs. Comprehensive cover, Add-ons).
Customer-first mindset with an ability to build rapport quickly.
Analytical thinking to generate insights from lead and sales data.
Ability to work independently as well as in a team-based environment.
Good command of spoken and written English and Hindi.
Basic proficiency in MS Excel, Google Sheets, and CRM software.

Qualification & Experience
Graduation (any stream) — MBA or relevant certification in insurance/sales is a plus.
Freshers – 4-5 years of experience in motor insurance telesales or general insurance sales preferred.
POSP / IRDAI certification preferred.

What We Offer
Attractive compensation structure with uncapped performance-based incentives.
Opportunity to work with one of the most trusted financial technology brands in India.
Growth-oriented environment with training and advancement opportunities.
Exposure to a wide network of digital distribution channels.

title: Intern - Talent Acquisition
description:
About Paytm
Paytm is India's leading mobile payments and financial services distribution company. Job Title
Talent Acquisition Intern – Non-Tech Recruitment

About the Role
As a Talent Acquisition Intern (Non-Tech), you will play an active role in driving talent identification and engagement across Paytm’s business, sales, operations, and corporate functions. Working closely with recruiters and business stakeholders, you will help source, screen, and coordinate candidates to fuel Paytm’s fast-paced growth.
This role is ideal for a proactive, energetic individual with strong communication skills, high learning agility, and an interest in modern, technology-enabled hiring practices. You will gain hands-on experience in end-to-end recruitment operations and candidate management in a high-volume fintech ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities
Candidate Sourcing: Leverage job boards, social channels, campus databases, and internal platforms to source qualified candidates for business, sales, and enabling function roles.
Screening & Assessment: Conduct initial resume screening and phone evaluations to assess candidate suitability, communication skills, and role alignment.
Interview Coordination: Manage end-to-end scheduling of interviews, candidate communications, and logistics to ensure a seamless candidate experience.
Pipeline Management: Maintain accurate candidate data and application stages across the Applicant Tracking System (ATS) and internal recruitment trackers.
Market Research: Perform basic market mapping and talent research to support recruiter search strategies for specialized non-tech profiles.
Process Automation & AI Adoption: Utilize modern sourcing tools, AI prompts, and automated communication platforms to speed up top-of-funnel hiring workflows.

Required Qualifications
Pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (MBA/PGDM in Human Resources or related fields preferred).
Strong written and verbal communication skills with an ability to engage candidates professionally.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail when managing multiple calendars and candidate pipelines.
High learning agility, curiosity, and comfort working in a fast-paced environment.
Basic proficiency in MS Office / Google Workspace (Sheets, Docs, Slides).
Preferred Qualifications
Prior internship experience in HR, recruitment, candidate sourcing, or talent coordination.
Familiarity with Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) and professional networking platforms like LinkedIn.
Interest in fintech, internet platforms, or high-growth technology environments.

AI Expectations
Sourcing & Search: Practical use of modern search methodologies and basic AI tools/prompts to quickly discover candidate profiles and boolean search strings.
Communication: Utilizing AI tools for drafting personalized candidate outreach messages, interview invitations, and follow-ups.
Productivity: Leveraging AI-driven tools and automation to summarize profiles, reduce administrative turnaround time, and improve daily recruitment throughput.

Ideal Candidate
Demonstrates Ownership & Bias for Action by taking initiative on daily sourcing and coordination tasks.
Exhibits Learning Agility with an eagerness to absorb recruiting best practices and stay open to new tools and ideas.
Displays Speed of Execution and adaptability in managing tight hiring schedules and candidate communication.
Strong focus on Candidate Experience and professional ethics.
